name: Pedro Álvares Cabral to Brazil and India
summary: The second fleet to India, thirteen ships, swings so far west into the Atlantic to catch the winds that on 22 April 1500 it sights a mountain: Brazil. Cabral claims the land for Portugal and sends a ship home with the news and Pero Vaz de Caminha's letter describing its people. Then he sails on: four ships are lost off the Cape, Bartolomeu Dias among the drowned, and at Calicut a fight with Arab merchants turns into a bombardment of the city.

stops.note: Thirteen ships sail in March, the largest fleet yet.
South to the islands, then far out to the west.
A mountain on the horizon, which he names Monte Pascoal; Tupinikin people meet them on the beach.
A storm sinks four ships; Bartolomeu Dias drowns off the cape he had rounded.
Up the east coast of Africa.
Pilots for the crossing to India.
A factory is attacked; Cabral bombards the city in reply.
A friendlier king, and full cargoes of pepper.
Home with half his fleet and a fortune in spice.
